my_time.title: My time

cannot_hand_in.month_running: The month is not over yet. It can be handed in once it has ended.
cannot_hand_in.timer_running: A timer is still running on one of your work items, in this or another workspace. Stop it, then hand the month in.

toasts.not_recomputed: Could not bring it up to date
toasts.handed_in_message: {month} is now waiting to be agreed.

my_time.no_record_detail: Your hours are not being tracked yet. If they should be, ask whoever looks after the team to set you up.
my_time.confirm_hand_in: Once {month} is handed in, you cannot change its hours, time off or attendance yourself. Ask whoever looks after the team if something needs correcting.

team_time.title: Team time
team_time.not_permitted: This is not yours to see
team_time.counted_anywhere: Everyone's hours are counted wherever they logged them, as hours and minutes: 161:12 means 161 hours and 12 minutes. The running balance only gets a figure once a month is closed. Closing a month freezes its figures; nothing recorded afterwards changes them.
team_time.as_things_stand: Figures are as things stand on {date}; the month is not over.
team_time.not_permitted_detail: Everyone's hours are only readable by whoever looks after the team. Your own month is on {page}.
team_time.confirm_close_body: The figures are frozen as they are now. Nobody can change this month's hours or absences afterwards, and anything recorded into it later will not count. The month can be reopened, and the reopening is recorded.

summary.as_of: As things stand on {date}. The month is not over.
summary.not_started: This month has not started yet.
summary.needs_review: Some days need looking at — hours that were counted before are no longer there. Whoever looks after the team has to settle them before the month can be closed.
summary.timer_running: A timer is still running on one of your work items, in this or another workspace. Stop it, then you can hand the month in.
summary.nothing_yet: Nothing has been worked out for this month yet.

day_table.not_yet: This day has not happened yet.
day_table.needs_review: Hours counted here earlier are no longer there
day_table.nothing_yet: Nothing has been worked out for this month yet.
day_table.rest_of_month: {count, plural, one {Show the rest of the month (# day)} other {Show the rest of the month (# days)}}
day_table.hide_rest_of_month: Hide the rest of the month

overview_table.nobody_yet: Nobody has an employment record yet. Add people on the People page and their hours start counting.
overview_table.timer_running: A timer is still running, so this month cannot be handed in yet.
overview_table.needs_review: Some days need looking at before this month can be closed
overview_table.month_running: The month is not over yet
overview_table.waiting_for: Waiting for {person} to hand the month in

reopen.title: Reopen {month}?
reopen.body: {person}'s month has been closed and its figures frozen. Reopening keeps the closed version and records this one alongside it — nothing that was agreed is overwritten.
reopen.label: Why is it being reopened?
reopen.placeholder: Three days in the second week were logged against the wrong month.

people.title: People
people.subtitle: Who the company employs, and the terms each of them works under.
people.nobody_yet: Nobody has an employment record yet. Add someone to start counting their hours.
people.footnote: Somebody who leaves is marked as having left rather than removed, so the months they worked stay readable.
people.not_permitted_detail: Only whoever looks after the team can change who is employed and on what terms.
people.add_hint: Pick the account whose hours this record will count.
people.everybody_added: Everybody already has an employment record.
people.modal_hint: Terms and a working week decide what this person's month comes to, so they are set together.
people.is_manager: Looks after the team — can see and change everyone's hours, absences and leave, in every workspace
people.records_target: Expect set hours each day, keep a running balance, and count the leave they take
people.records_target_hint: Leave this on for employees. Turn it off for anyone who invoices us for their own hours: no hours are expected of them each day, no balance is kept and no leave is counted.
people.schedule_hint: How long each day should be. Type 7:42 for seven hours and 42 minutes, or 7.7 for the same length written as decimal hours. Leave a day blank when it is not worked.

errors.bad_duration: One of the days is not a length of time. Type 7:42 or 7.7, or leave it blank.
errors.hire_date_required: Say when this person started, so their first month knows where to begin.
errors.week_required: Fill in at least one day, so their month has something to be measured against. Leave the days they do not work blank.
errors.bad_crm_staff_id: A CRM staff id is a whole number. Leave it empty to match on the email address instead.

people.crm_staff_id_placeholder: Leave empty to match by email

crm_link.set: Set here, so the hours go to this account whatever the addresses say.
crm_link.email: Nobody has said which CRM account this is, so their hours are matched on the email address. Nothing checks that a CRM account with that address exists.
crm_link.none: Nothing joins this person to the CRM, so their hours never become a CRM timer.

people.confirm_remove_body: {person} stops appearing in new months and can no longer open their own time page, so finish their last month before this. Everything already recorded stays as it is.
people.confirm_remove_permanent: You can employ them again later if they come back.
people.pick_somebody_first: Pick somebody from the list first
people.nobody_matches_detail: Only people who already have an account here can be given an employment record. Accounts are created in Workspace settings, under Members.
people.everybody_added_detail: Everyone with an account here already has an employment record.

entries.hint: Hours that are not on a work item — meetings, admin, training, travel. They count towards your month. Hours on work items come from the timers there and are not changed here.
entries.none_yet: Nothing has been added here yet. Hours recorded on work items are counted, but are not shown here.
entries.note_placeholder: What this time was spent on
entries.month_closed: This month is no longer open, so its hours cannot be changed. Ask whoever looks after the team to reopen it if something needs correcting.

errors.bad_duration: Say how long it was. Type 1:30 or 1.5.
errors.duration_needs_unit: Say how long it was: 1:30, 7h, or 90m. A number on its own does not say whether you mean hours or minutes.

entries.not_added_yet: Not added yet. Press Add, or it is lost when you close.
entries.confirm_remove_body: {duration} of {category} comes off this day and off the month's total.

attendance.title: When you were at work
attendance.hint: Start, end and breaks for this day. It is a separate record and does not count towards your hours.
attendance.closed_with: {from} to {to}, {duration}. This month is no longer open, so it cannot be changed.
attendance.closed_without: Nothing was recorded for this day, and the month is no longer open.

errors.bad_break: Give the break in whole minutes.

attendance.confirm_remove_body: The start, end and break for this day are removed and cannot be brought back. If the times are wrong, change them and save instead.
attendance.past_midnight_length: This runs past midnight and comes to {duration}. Check the end time if that is not right.
attendance.not_saved_yet: Not saved yet. Save these times, or they are lost when you close.

imports.title: Bring earlier records in
imports.subtitle: Hours, absences and balances recorded somewhere else, read from a spreadsheet and checked before anything is written. In a workbook, only the sheet it opens on is read, and the column headings must be its first row.
imports.not_permitted_detail: Only whoever looks after the team can bring earlier records in.

columns.time_entries: Columns: email, date, and either hours or minutes — those exact headings. A note column is kept if there is one. The heading decides what a plain number means: 7.7 under hours and 462 under minutes are both 7 hours 42 minutes. Written as 7:42 it is the same under either heading.
columns.absences: Columns: email, start_date, end_date and type — those exact headings. Leave end_date out for a single day.
columns.opening_balances: Columns: email, date for the day the balance applies from, either hours or minutes for the balance itself, and basis saying where the figure came from — those exact headings. Add a kind column saying time, leave or overtime if the balance is not hours.

imports.preview_hint: Nothing has been written yet. Rows are added to whatever is already recorded for those days, so a day brought in twice counts twice. To correct a file that is already in, undo it first instead of bringing in a corrected copy.
imports.none_yet: Nothing has been brought in yet.
imports.row_summary: {total, plural, one {{valid} of # row can be used} other {{valid} of # rows can be used}}
imports.undo_body: Everything this file wrote is taken back out, and nothing else is touched. If any of it has been counted into a month that is now closed, nothing is taken out until that month is reopened.

toasts.written: {count, plural, one {# row written} other {# rows written}}
toasts.removed: {count, plural, one {# row removed} other {# rows removed}}

reasons.unknown_person: Nobody here logs in as {email}. Add the person under People, or correct the address in the file.
reasons.bad_date: The date could not be read.
reasons.bad_duration: The amount of time could not be read, or it is zero. Every row needs a length of time — leave the day out of the file instead.
reasons.more_than_a_day: That is more than 24 hours in one day. Check whether the number is hours or minutes, and that the column heading matches.
reasons.month_settled: That month is no longer open, so nothing more can go into it. Ask for it to be reopened if this has to go in.
reasons.bad_balance: The balance could not be read.
reasons.kind_missing: The kind column must say time, leave or overtime.
reasons.basis_missing: The basis column is empty. Write where the figure came from, for example: from the old leave spreadsheet.
reasons.bad_start_date: The start date could not be read.
reasons.unknown_absence_type: No reason for being away has the code “{code}”. The codes are on the Absences screen, under Reasons.

opening.title: {person}'s starting balance
opening.hint: Where this person stood on the day counting started here. There is no history to work these out from, which is why they are agreed rather than derived — so each one keeps what it was based on, and the person it belongs to says whether they accept it.
opening.none_yet: No starting balance has been recorded yet, so counting begins from zero.
opening.replaced: {count, plural, one {# replaced by a correction} other {# replaced by a correction}}
opening.amount: Balance, minus if they are behind
opening.basis_placeholder: Carried over from the leave spreadsheet, checked against the March payslip

errors.bad_duration: Say how much. Type -12:30 or -12.5, or leave off the minus for a surplus.
errors.basis_required: Say what this figure is based on. A number nobody can account for is one nobody can defend when the person it belongs to disagrees.
errors.date_required: Say which day this balance applies from.

opening.confirm_agree_body: You are agreeing that {amount} is right. This cannot be taken back. If the figure is wrong, do not agree to it — say so to whoever looks after the team.

absences.title: Absences
absences.subtitle: Time away from work, and what it does to the month.
absences.none_this_month: No absences recorded for this month.
absences.not_permitted_detail: There is no employment record for you here, so there is nothing to show. Ask whoever looks after the team to set one up.
absences.month_locked: month closed — reopen it to change this

granularity.hours: A set number of hours a day

modal.title: Record an absence
modal.subtitle: Most reasons still count towards the hours for the month, so the month does not come out short. Days this person does not normally work are not counted.
modal.backwards: The last day cannot come before the first.
modal.hours_hint: Hours on each day of the range, written as 3:30, 3.5 or 3h. For minutes write 90m.
modal.hours_unreadable: That is not a length of time. Try 3:30, 3.5, or 90m for ninety minutes.

types.title: Reasons for being away
types.subtitle: Two answers decide the arithmetic: whether the day still counts as worked, and whether it comes off the leave account.
types.counts_as_worked: The day still counts as worked
types.draws_on_leave: The day comes off the leave account
types.confirm_remove_body: “{kind}” will no longer be offered when somebody records an absence. Press Retire instead if you only want it out of the list.

absences.confirm_remove_body: {duration} stops counting towards {person}'s month, so the month will be short unless those hours are worked. Any leave this used goes back.
absences.refuse_body: This is kept with the record. Nobody is told automatically, so tell them yourself as well.
absences.refuse_placeholder: Two people are already away that week

rates.title: What {person}'s time is worth
rates.hint: Rates are kept by date, so a month already worked out keeps the rate it used. To record a raise, add a rate starting on the day it takes effect. It takes over from the one before it, which goes on pricing the months before that.
rates.none_yet: No rate on record. A statement for this person will show hours and no amount.

errors.date_required: Say which day this rate starts.
errors.bad_amount: Write the amount as a number, like 65 or 65.50.

rates.confirm_remove_body: Every month is priced from the rate on record at the moment it is read, months already closed included. Deleting this changes what those months come to. Delete it only if it was recorded by mistake.

statement.title: Before you invoice
statement.hint: What this month comes to at your rate, so the figure is agreed before the invoice is written rather than argued about after it arrives.
statement.no_rate: No rate on record for you yet, so this shows the hours only. Ask whoever looks after the team.
statement.still_moving: This month is not closed yet, so these figures can still move. Wait until it is closed before you invoice.
statement.settled: The month is closed, so these figures are settled.

leave.title: {person}'s leave
leave.hint: Leave is counted in hours, not days, because a working day is not the same length for everyone. The leave year runs from the anniversary of joining.
leave.none_yet: No leave year on record yet.
leave.carryover_placeholder: Optional. Use a minus if they have already taken some of it.

errors.dates_required: Say when the leave year starts and ends.
errors.backwards: The leave year cannot end before it starts.
errors.already_there: There is already an entry for this leave year.
errors.overlapping_year: There is already a leave year covering these dates.

leave.confirm_agree_body: {duration} can no longer be changed on any screen afterwards. Check it against what the person was told before you hold it.

holidays.title: Public holidays
holidays.subtitle: The days nobody works. A holiday counts as hours worked; it does not lower what somebody has to work. A change here only reaches months that are still open.
holidays.none_this_year: No days for this year yet. Until they are added, every public holiday in it counts as an ordinary working day.
holidays.not_permitted_detail: You are not set up in the time records yet, so this list is not shown to you. Ask whoever looks after the team.
holidays.add: Add a day off for everyone

errors.date_and_name: Give the day a date and a name.

holidays.confirm_remove_body: {day} stops being a holiday. Everybody who works that day is expected to work it again.

shared.load_failed_detail: Something went wrong on the way. Try again, and tell whoever looks after the team if it keeps happening.

review_days.title: Days to look at for {person}
review_days.body: Hours that were counted on these days are no longer there. Writing down what happened lets the month be closed, but it does not put the hours back — if they should still count, have them recorded again first. What you write is kept with the day, and the person it is about can read it.
review_days.all_settled: Nothing left to look at. This month can be closed.
review_days.placeholder: Entered on the wrong day and moved

refusals.absence_type_in_use: {in_use, plural, one {# absence is recorded with this reason, so it cannot be deleted — the record of it would stop making sense.} other {# absences are recorded with this reason, so it cannot be deleted — the record of them would stop making sense.}} Press Retire instead: it disappears from the list of reasons somebody can choose, and the existing ones stay readable.
refusals.month_settled: {month} has been {month_state}, so its records can no longer change. Ask whoever looks after the team to reopen it on Team time.
refusals.last_manager: This is the only person who looks after the team. Taking it away would leave nobody able to reach anyone's month, and nobody able to give it back. Make somebody else a manager first.

detail.title: Hours in detail
detail.frozen_hint: These hours can no longer change
detail.still_running: Still running — it has no length yet and counts nothing
detail.gone: This entry was deleted after the month counted it. Its hours are still in the figures above.
detail.nothing_logged: No hours were recorded on a work item in this month. Check the month shown at the top.
detail.other_subtitle: Meetings, administration, training, travel, corrections — and hours brought in from somewhere else. They count in the month too, but they are not in the table above. A correction with a minus sign takes hours off the month.
detail.footnote: Hours are counted wherever they were logged, in every workspace. Paid leave and public holidays also count towards the month, and are not shown here.
detail.rounding_note: Each day's hours on a project are rounded once, so adding these lines up can come out a minute or two from the figure above. The figure above is the one that counts.
detail.running_note: {count, plural, one {# timer is still running, so it counts nothing yet. Stop it on the work item. The month cannot be handed in while it runs.} other {# timers are still running, so they count nothing yet. Stop them on the work items. The month cannot be handed in while they run.}}
detail.missing_note: {count, plural, one {# entry this month counted has since been deleted. Its hours are not in the figures here, but the month still counts them.} other {# entries this month counted have since been deleted. Their hours are not in the figures here, but the month still counts them.}}
detail.auto_stopped: · stopped by the system, needs correcting
detail.auto_stopped_hint: This timer was left running, so the system stopped it at the longest time it allows. That is a limit, not time that was worked. Correct it on the work item before the month is handed in.
